permutationLabel: Elderly, chronic, thiazide + SSRI, moderately severe symptoms
summary: 82-year-old woman on bendroflumethiazide and newly started sertraline with nausea, confusion and a fall; sodium 119, potassium 3.1, euvolaemic.

inputs.hpi: Bendroflumethiazide for years; sertraline started 3 weeks ago for low mood. Four days of nausea, poor appetite, unsteadiness and new confusion; fell at home today without head injury. Drinking normally.

exam.general: Mildly confused (AMT 6/10). Clinically euvolaemic: moist mucous membranes, no postural drop, no oedema. Pulse 84/min, BP 134/72, RR 16, temperature 36.6°C.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Chronic hyponatraemia with moderately severe symptoms (thiazide and SSRI)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Chronic euvolaemic hyponatraemia (Na 119) with moderately severe symptoms from thiazide and sertraline; hypokalaemia 3.1; high osmotic demyelination risk with rapid correction.

redFlags.note: Potassium replacement raises sodium too: part of the overcorrection risk.
redFlags.knownGapNote: Web: Potassium 3.1 is not flagged: there is no hypokalaemia prompt.
redFlags.proposedFix: Add a hypokalaemia prompt, and warn that correcting potassium raises sodium.

mustInclude.note: Graded as management because the web prompt adds this test as a plan line, not an investigation order.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web: Only "Review medications for SIADH causes: diuretics, SSRIs, carbamazepine" — the thiazide is framed as an SIADH cause and never stopped.
mustInclude.proposedFix: When a thiazide is on the medication list and Na <130, add "stop the thiazide".

mustInclude.note: Elderly, chronic, hypokalaemic, thiazide: high risk of osmotic demyelination with rapid correction.
Moderately severe symptoms: a single 150 mL 3% infusion (European 2014).

guideline.name: European clinical practice guideline on diagnosis and treatment of hyponatraemia (ESE/ESICM/ERBP)
guideline.section: Severe symptoms (seizure, vomiting, reduced consciousness): 150 mL 3% hypertonic saline over 20 min, repeated (up to twice) checking sodium, target +5 mmol/L; moderately severe symptoms: single 150 mL 3% infusion; limit the rise to 10 mmol/L in the first 24 h and 8 mmol/L in each subsequent 24 h; hypovolaemic hyponatraemia: restore volume with 0.9% saline or balanced crystalloid; SIADH: fluid restriction first line; stop contributing drugs
guideline.citation: Spasovski G, Vanholder R, Allolio B, et al. Clinical practice guideline on diagnosis and treatment of hyponatraemia. Eur J Endocrinol. 2014;170:G1–47.

rationale: Chronic hyponatraemia in an older woman: stop the causative drugs and correct slowly (limit 10 mmol/L in 24 h).
